comment: What each job and each of its named steps actually covers.
This exists because the answer used to be spread across a thousand lines of
YAML, and nothing compared two steps that named overlapping suites. A suite
listed twice for one platform is duplicate execution; a guarantee listed
nowhere is a guarantee no job is holding. `validate-ci-coverage.lua` checks
this file against the workflow and against tests/groups.lua on every run,
before anything expensive is provisioned, so it cannot go quietly stale.
`suites` and `groups` name what a step runs. `guarantees` name what it is
for, in the words the plan and the release notes use.

steps.name: Check C formatting
guarantees: adopted Nupp C sources and headers match the pinned formatters

steps.name: Lint C
guarantees: adopted Nupp C sources and headers pass the pinned clang-tidy

steps.name: Classify the affected surfaces
guarantees: every change selects the jobs that can observe it

steps.name: Validate selected-job aggregation
guarantees: a selected correctness job cannot pass by being skipped or absent

steps.name: Validate the workflow against the classifier
guarantees: the classifier, this map and the workflow name the same jobs

steps.name: Build the compiler
guarantees: the compiler builds from these sources, once, for every Linux job that runs it

steps.name: Build the compiler
guarantees: the compiler builds from these sources, once, for every macOS leg

steps.name: Build the compiler
guarantees: the compiler builds from these sources, once, for every Windows leg

steps.name: Build the test runner
guarantees: the manifest's test runner builds from these sources, once, for every Linux leg

steps.name: Build the test runner
guarantees: the manifest's test runner builds from these sources, once, for every macOS leg

steps.name: Build the test runner
guarantees: the manifest's test runner builds from these sources, once, for every Windows leg

steps.name: Check the formatting
guarantees: committed source is what nupp fmt --write produces

steps.name: Check the compiler
guarantees: the compiler type-checks its own sources
committed source spells module paths as imports

comment: The three integration jobs run one list of steps, written once here and
aliased by the other two, so a step's platforms are named on the step.

steps.name: Check the compiler
guarantees: the checker's answer is not platform-dependent

steps.name: Run the Windows native and launcher preflight
guarantees: the Windows Rust host ABI contract
a Windows loader failure names its last case

steps.name: Gate the Rust-native platform artifacts
guarantees: resource owner stress and cancellation

steps.name: Run the native core suites
guarantees: the handler sources lower, compile and pass the native contract tests

steps.name: Run the bridge under the sanitizers
guarantees: the core bridge's C passes its contracts and representative guests under ASan and UBSan

steps.name: Run the core guests and units
guarantees: every core guest case and runtime unit runs on the core in normal and spill mode against its inventoried baseline

steps.name: Run the benchmark runner suite
guarantees: the benchmark runner's process boundary: listing, selection, replication and the pilot

steps.name: Run the tl.lua oracle and import-c fixtures
guarantees: the external parser oracle and the C importer

steps.name: Run the compiler suite
guarantees: standalone programs exchange owned channel messages across cooperative tasks and worker VMs

steps.name: Run the compiler suite
guarantees: every suite no group-named step of this job runs, each lane dealt across shards that partition it

steps.name: Verify the self-hosting fixpoint
guarantees: the compiler rebuilds itself byte-identically from stage zero

steps.name: Regenerate and verify the documentation
guarantees: generated documentation matches its sources
every diagnostic code has a reference section
every documented Nupp example checks, or is marked a fragment or a refused program

steps.name: Run exact GPU dispatch and readback
guarantees: exact Vulkan dispatch and readback on a software adapter

steps.name: Run exact DX12 dispatch and readback
guarantees: exact DX12 dispatch and readback

steps.name: Run the C proofs
guarantees: CBMC verifies the bounded contracts for the bundle header, HTTP ring and response-header packer, Markdown allocation budget, file I/O tickets, and TCP buffer ownership and close

steps.name: Require every selected job to have succeeded
guarantees: one stable status whose meaning survives job reorganization

steps.name: Record the run
guarantees: queue time, execution time, conclusion and revision are retained
